chief_complaint: Management of cardiometabolic risk (type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, obesity)
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 62-year-old male with a longstanding history of obesity (BMI ≥ 30 since 1983) who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus and metabolic syndrome in May 2020. Hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, and hyperglycemia were documented in May 2021. Laboratory data show a recent HbA1c of 6.7%, indicating borderline glycemic control. Blood pressure, lipid panel, BMI, and renal function values are missing, limiting assessment of control. He has chronic anemia of unknown etiology and reports ongoing stress. Socially, he works part‑time, has a criminal record, and completed only high‑school education. Preventive eye imaging for diabetic retinopathy has been performed repeatedly (2020‑2023), but outpatient visits for chronic disease management have been sparse (only 2 in the last three years). Current therapy includes low‑dose metformin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide, with no statin or other lipid‑lowering agents.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include viral sinusitis (2022), acute viral pharyngitis (2022), a colon polyp removed in 2022, prior reports of environmental violence (resolved 2021), earlier medication review prompts (resolved 2019 and 2017), full‑time employment (ended 2021), social isolation (resolved 2019), and two lacerations of the thigh (resolved 2016).
